skill.name: api-designer
skill.description: Design REST and GraphQL APIs with OpenAPI specifications, authentication guidance, versioning strategies, documentation patterns, and a small local helper script.
skill.summary: Create API contracts, schemas, authentication plans, and documentation workflows.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, OpenAPI examples, example URLs, sample secrets, and normal validation text. The only confirmed issue is that scripts/api_helper.py writes user-supplied output paths, which can overwrite writable local files when executed with unsafe arguments. No prompt-injection attempts, hidden network exfiltration, or malicious intent were found.

remediation.issue: User-supplied output paths can overwrite local files.
remediation.suggestion: Validate output paths, warn before overwriting existing files, and document that the helper script writes only user-approved files.

remediation.issue: Example credentials resemble real API keys.
remediation.suggestion: Replace sample secrets with obvious placeholders such as <api_key> and <webhook_secret> to reduce scanner noise and copy-paste risk.

remediation.issue: Helper script execution is optional but not strongly bounded in documentation.
remediation.suggestion: State that users should review command arguments and run the script only in a trusted project directory.

content.value_statement: API teams need consistent contracts before implementation begins. This skill guides REST, GraphQL, OpenAPI, authentication, versioning, and documentation decisions.
actual_capabilities: Design REST resources, methods, status codes, pagination, filtering, and error responses.
Draft GraphQL types, queries, mutations, inputs, and resolver guidance.
Create OpenAPI 3.0 specification structures with schemas, servers, paths, and security schemes.
Select authentication patterns, including OAuth 2.0, JWT, API keys, RBAC, and rate limits.
Plan API versioning, deprecation timelines, migration notices, and backward compatibility rules.
Use a local Python helper to generate sample specs, validate specs, and create Markdown docs.
limitations: It provides design guidance and examples, not a complete API implementation.
The helper script supports sample generation, validation, and Markdown output only.
Security advice must be adapted to each platform, threat model, and compliance requirement.
Generated contracts still need review by backend, frontend, security, and product owners.

use_cases.title: Define a New Product API
use_cases.description: Map resources, endpoints, payloads, authentication, and error responses before backend development starts.

use_cases.title: Standardize API Governance
use_cases.description: Create shared rules for status codes, versioning, documentation, pagination, and deprecation notices.

use_cases.title: Improve Developer Documentation
use_cases.description: Turn an OpenAPI specification into clear reference material with examples and authentication notes.

prompt_templates.title: Start a REST Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple REST API contract.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a REST API for [product area]. Include resources, methods, request fields, response fields, status codes, and pagination.

prompt_templates.title: Create an OpenAPI Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an OpenAPI outline for [service]. Include servers, paths, schemas, security schemes, common errors, and example operations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend an authentication and authorization design for [API]. Compare OAuth 2.0, JWT, API keys, scopes, roles, rate limits, and token rotation.

prompt_templates.title: Review an API Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this API contract for consistency, breaking changes, GraphQL or REST design issues, versioning risk, security gaps, and documentation gaps: [contract summary].

output_examples.input: Design a REST API for managing blog posts and comments.
output_examples.output: A resource map with post and comment endpoints, method choices, status codes, pagination rules, validation errors, and authentication requirements.

output_examples.input: Plan versioning for a public API that will replace user fields.
output_examples.output: A migration plan with compatibility rules, deprecation headers, timeline guidance, communication steps, and client migration notes.

output_examples.input: Review our GraphQL schema for performance risks.
output_examples.output: A review covering query shape, resolver boundaries, input design, pagination, authorization checks, and N plus one prevention.

best_practices: Start with resources, user workflows, and error cases before writing endpoint details.
Keep authentication, authorization, rate limits, and audit needs visible in the contract.
Review generated specifications with every team that consumes or operates the API.
anti_patterns: Do not expose secrets in query parameters or example requests.
Do not create version changes without migration guidance and deprecation timelines.
Do not treat generated documentation as final without human review.

faq.question: Does this skill support REST and GraphQL?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes REST workflow guidance, GraphQL schema patterns, examples, and review prompts.

faq.question: Can it create a complete OpenAPI specification?
faq.answer: It can guide specification structure and provide examples. Final accuracy depends on your service details.

faq.question: Does the helper script make network requests?
faq.answer: No. The script generates, validates, and writes local specification or documentation files.

faq.question: Is it suitable for security-sensitive APIs?
faq.answer: It includes authentication and authorization guidance, but security teams should review production designs.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users review before running commands?
faq.answer: Review file paths, output locations, and existing files because the helper script can write local files.
